end.summary:
Practised how earthworms and other soil animals help soil.
Pihu explained that earthworm tunnels let in air and water and that soil animals help turn dead leaves into rich soil, with prompting.
Practised naming soil and leaf-litter animals: earthworm, ant, beetle, millipede, woodlouse, and termite; names were not recalled unaided.
Pihu initially called earthworms insects and said they spoil soil; the insect mix-up was corrected later by focusing on legs (correctAfterLastSeen: 1).
end.parentNote: Asha practised this with examples and questions about tunnels, air, water, and dead leaves. Pihu used the idea that earthworms mix leaves into soil and make it richer after discussion. They mixed up earthworms with insects and thought earthworms spoil soil; this was corrected later by checking whether earthworms have legs. At home, look at a picture of soil animals and sort them into “insects” and “not insects,” then name one way each helps soil.
